boundary: comprehensive: accelerators, host CPU and memory, idle capacity, and data-center overhead (PUE)
interval: low and high are each parameter's plausible bounds, treated as a ~90% interval

output_wh_per_1k.opus.label: MODELED
output_wh_per_1k.opus.note: Largest tier. Scaled up from the Sonnet value; Anthropic does not disclose model size or energy. Bounds cover published per-token estimates for frontier models.

output_wh_per_1k.sonnet.label: MODELED
output_wh_per_1k.sonnet.note: Anchored so a typical chat query (about 1k input, 400 output tokens) lands near Google's measured 0.24 Wh median Gemini prompt and the 0.34 Wh median frontier query (IQR 0.18-0.67). Third-party estimates for Claude output run 0.4-2 Wh per 1k.

output_wh_per_1k.haiku.label: GUESS
output_wh_per_1k.haiku.note: Smallest tier. Scaled down from Sonnet roughly in line with the price gap between tiers, which is a weak proxy for compute.

input_vs_output.label: MODELED
input_vs_output.note: Energy of one fresh input token relative to one output token. Input is processed in parallel (prefill), so it costs less per token. Anthropic prices input at 1/5 of output; a Watershed-based estimate uses about 1/3.

cache_write_vs_input.label: MODELED
cache_write_vs_input.note: Writing to the cache means processing the tokens fresh, then storing the result. Priced at 1.25x input.

cache_read_vs_input.label: MODELED
cache_read_vs_input.note: The parameter that matters most for agents, where cache reads are 90%+ of tokens. Hausfather's central case is 10% of fresh input, tested at 1% and 25%. Anthropic prices cache reads at 0.1x input.

ev_kwh_per_mile.label: MEASURED
ev_kwh_per_mile.note: Typical EV uses 25-35 kWh per 100 miles (EPA).

fridge_kwh_per_day.label: MEASURED
fridge_kwh_per_day.note: A typical US refrigerator uses about 400-600 kWh a year.

us_home_kwh_per_day.label: MEASURED
us_home_kwh_per_day.note: Average US household used about 10,800 kWh in a year (EIA).
